context: A scatter chart (salary vs. experience, 60 points, 5 categories) rendered simultaneously at 6 container sizes — Full (640px), Simplified (380px, 300px), Sparkline (180px), and KPI (130px, 80px) — as a demo of CSS container queries with linked cross-panel hover highlighting.
first_impression: Purposeful and readable — the six panels read as one progressive-disclosure concept rather than six independent views, keeping cognitive load low despite the visual density.
what_works: The five-color TOL palette cleanly separates all categories across every panel size; the mode badges (FULL / SIMPLIFIED / SPARKLINE / KPI) immediately orient the viewer to the progressive-disclosure logic so the layout tells its own story.
what_doesnt: The bottom row's height inconsistency — the 300px simplified panel is roughly 3× taller than the KPI panels beside it — makes the row feel misaligned and undercuts the demo's polish; the 80px KPI panel wraps '$4,494/yr exp' mid-phrase, breaking readability at the very size where only summary text survives.
